rationale:
#917: a MACRO-WRAPPED heading — `MACRO(ret, name)(params){ body }`. The heading stands where the declaration specifier belongs and is CALL-shaped, so the published grammar reads it as `MACRO(ret, name)` CALLED with `(params)` and leaves the body as an ORPHAN `compound_statement` (a direct child of the translation_unit, or of the ERROR / preproc_ifdef that swallowed the region). No `function_definition` exists, so the definition was never a symbol, its locals were published as FILE-SCOPE names, and every read in its body was attributed to `global`. Measured on sqlite: 235 such definitions across ext/wasm/libcmpp.c (86) and ext/jni/src/c/sqlite3-jni.c (149). MEASURED THROUGH THE PRODUCTION ENTRY, pre-fix vs post-fix, only `src/ast/real-c-analyzer.ts` differing. PRE-FIX symbols (8): cmpp_size_t@30, helperTarget@32, fileScope@34, `enum_member:BufSize@42`, `enum:anonymous_enum@42`, plain_stream@53, plain_control@78, helper_defined@83 — i.e. `cmpp_stream`, `1value_1text` and `cmpp_err_set` did NOT exist at all, and the wrapped body's anonymous enum leaked as a FILE-SCOPE symbol. PRE-FIX edges included `uses global->BufSize@43` and `contains anonymous_enum->BufSize@42` (the tree-truth oracle cannot derive either — that pair is the single unexplained row the whole 315-file sqlite c lane carried) and all three wrapped bodies' calls attributed to FILE SCOPE (`calls global->helperTarget@47/66/72`). POST-FIX: the three definitions exist as `function` symbols with their scope, return type and parameters, the leaked enum and its read are gone, and the same calls are attributed to the functions that make them (`calls cmpp_stream->helperTarget@47`, `calls 1value_1text->helperTarget@66`, `calls cmpp_err_set->helperTarget@72`). The three spellings are pinned because each reads the heading's own structure, never the source line: `(int, cmpp_stream)` — the declared name is the macro's LAST argument and the return type is the first comma-separated one; `S3JniApi(existing_binding(),jstring,1value_1text)` — the name is the THIRD argument and the lexer SPLITS it (`1` + `value_1text`) because an identifier cannot start with a digit, so the fragment is rejoined on adjacency; `CMPP__EXPORT(int, cmpp_err_set)( int rc, char const * zFmt, ... )` — a variadic list, where the grammar's recovery swallows the remaining parameters into one ERROR token, so the parameter payload is HONESTLY PARTIAL (only the variadic marker) while the definition itself is fully recovered. The CONTROLS carry the other half of the contract: `plain_stream` is the same body in an ORDINARY function (its enum must not leak either, and pre-fix it did not — the wrapped case now matches it), and `plain_control` is a call chain followed by a block INSIDE a function, which is two statements and must never become a definition (the recovery is gated on the scope, so no symbol is emitted for it and the call keeps its own attribution). NOT pinned, and merely declared: `calls global->CMPP__EXPORT@40` and `@71` are the call-shaped reading of the macro INVOCATION itself — measured IDENTICAL pre-fix and post-fix, a pre-existing artifact of the same grammar accident, so they are not enshrined here. NOT part of this class and deliberately absent: a heading whose macro's first argument is a POINTER type (`CMPP__EXPORT(void *, cmpp_mrealloc)(...){...}`, 6 sites in libcmpp.c) — there the heading parses as a DECLARATION that names the macro, so no orphan body exists at all; measured PRE-FIX and POST-FIX IDENTICAL and registered as its own defect.

#961 SUPERSEDES PART OF THIS FIXTURE. The three forbids above -- `BufSize`, `PlainSize`, `anonymous_enum` -- recorded the harm CGD20 was papering over rather than the behaviour C wanted: they forbid a local enum's members from being published AT ALL, which is right when they would be owned by a placeholder and wrong once the type is qualified. They are replaced by positive rows asserting the correct shape, and the two unrelated forbids (`CMPP__EXPORT`, `S3JniApi` -- macro-mediated and phantom names) are untouched.

expectSymbols.name: BufSize
expectSymbols.note: #961: a function-local type is published, QUALIFIED by its enclosing function. CGD20 dropped these as 'execution artifacts' and this fixture's forbids recorded the harm that dropping was papering over: an anonymous local enum published as the PLACEHOLDER `anonymous_enum` with `BufSize` and `PlainSize` owned by that name, which resolves to nothing -- two symbols with one name in one file, and file-scope EnumMembers. Qualifying the type fixes the leak at its CAUSE: the members are now owned by `cmpp_stream` / `plain_stream`, both real symbols. Owned by the enclosing function's enum, not by a placeholder and not file-scope.

CGD20 dropped these as 'execution artifacts' and this fixture's forbids recorded the harm that dropping was papering over: an anonymous local enum published as the PLACEHOLDER `anonymous_enum` with `BufSize` and `PlainSize` owned by that name, which resolves to nothing -- two symbols with one name in one file, and file-scope EnumMembers. the declared NAME is a declaration, never a read — the heading's naming argument must not resolve against the symbol the recovery mints (measured: without this, the LATER heading's own name fabricated `uses` once an earlier site emitted the symbol — order-dependent).
